profile.headline: Data Engineer
profile.summary:
I'm a Mathematics and Computer Science graduate from Washington University in St. Louis, currently seeking Machine Learning Engineer and Applied AI roles.

I'm a Research Software Engineer at WashU's DI2 Accelerator, fine-tuning transformer models (Clinical-Longformer) on clinical notes to identify patient social risk factors. I work daily in Python, PyTorch, HuggingFace, and SQL, and use Claude Code extensively for model evaluation and pipeline development.

Previously: Data Analyst at Bunzl (Python, SQLite automation) and two summers teaching 8th-grade math at Breakthrough San Francisco. I've also independently built an on-device AI system, a privacy-first iOS baby monitor with real-time inference and end-to-end encryption.

Looking for ML Engineer / Applied AI roles, and I am open to relocation.

positions.title: Research Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
-Fine-tuned a multi-head transformer classifier over Clinical-Longformer to detect eight social risk factor domains in clinical notes.
-Built a GPT-based annotation pipeline to generate training labels for previously unlabeled clinical notes, enabling large-scale model training.

positions.title: Data Analyst
positions.description:
-Migrated packaging material weight reporting workflows from Excel to Python and SQLite to handle growing datasets, automating report generation for state government EPR compliance.
-Integrated data validation pipelines to ensure accuracy of final datasets submitted to Operating Companies for regulatory review and sign-off.

positions.title: Returning Teaching Fellow
positions.description:
-Taught linear relationships, systems of equations, and problem-solving strategies in an interactive classroom.
-Designed hands-on, discussion-based lessons that increased student engagement and confidence.
-Served as an academic mentor and advisor for a cohort of middle-school students.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant for CSE 417T: Introduction to Machine Learning
positions.description:
-Held office hours to support students with model training, evaluation, and Python implementation.
-Created grading rubrics and assessed homework, exams, and ML projects.

projects.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence to Reduce Patient Social Risks and Improve Health
projects.description: Comparing a fine-tuned multi-head transformer classifier against an LLM API for automated screening of Social Determinants of Health (SDoH)

projects.title: Classroom Assistant LLM
projects.description: Collaborated with Cloudera, utilizing their external environment and GPU/CPU computing power to customize a Microsoft Phi-3 Mini LLM for WashU’s CSE 332 course, integrating lecture transcriptions, large coding standard databases, and course materials. Developed a REST API that made calls to our model for automatic responses to student Piazza posts, utilizing eigenvector similarity for efficient query handling.
